items.stem: A 45-year-old has two separate in-office readings consistent with stage 1 hypertension and no end-organ damage. What is a guideline-consistent initial step?

options.text: Confirm with out-of-office/repeat measurement and initiate lifestyle modification, considering risk-based pharmacologic therapy
options.rationale: Correct: confirming the diagnosis and starting lifestyle change, with pharmacotherapy based on cardiovascular risk, is guideline-consistent.
Triple therapy at first presentation of uncomplicated stage 1 hypertension is not guideline-consistent.
Elevated readings require assessment and management, not dismissal.
Stage 1 hypertension without emergency features is managed in primary care, not surgically.

items.explanation: Correct: confirming the diagnosis and starting lifestyle change, with pharmacotherapy based on cardiovascular risk, is guideline-consistent.

items.stem: Why may medication dosing need adjustment in older adults?

options.text: Age-related changes in renal/hepatic function and body composition alter drug handling
options.rationale: Correct: pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic changes with age affect dosing and risk.

options.text: Older adults never metabolise any drugs
options.rationale: They still metabolise drugs, though often differently; dosing is adjusted, not eliminated.

options.text: Dosing is identical to paediatric dosing
options.rationale: Adult geriatric dosing is not the same as paediatric dosing.

options.text: Age has no effect on drug handling
options.rationale: Age clearly affects pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics.

items.explanation: Correct: pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic changes with age affect dosing and risk.

items.stem: Select TWO responsibilities that fall within an FNP's professional role and ethics.

options.text: Practising within the legal scope defined by the relevant jurisdiction
options.rationale: Correct: practising within the jurisdiction's scope is a core professional responsibility.

options.text: Referring when a patient's needs exceed the FNP's scope or competence
options.rationale: Correct: timely referral when needs exceed scope/competence is a professional duty.

options.text: Prescribing outside legal authority to save time
options.rationale: Prescribing beyond legal authority is outside scope and unethical.
Informed consent is an ethical obligation, not optional.

options.text: Guaranteeing a cure for every patient
options.rationale: Guaranteeing cures is neither possible nor ethical.

items.explanation: Correct: practising within the jurisdiction's scope is a core professional responsibility.
